reason: Dev-only dependencies (zstd-jni, lmdbjava) and bench sources must stay out of the shipped NeoForge and Fabric jars. An empty grep proves absence only after a positive control, so the check needs both.
Mixins compile but are only applied at runtime if the refmap in the jar lists them. This skill is the jar-inspection skill, so the refmap check belongs here, and the trigger must name it.
Adds the concrete step that proved a new client mixin reached the Fabric jar. Positive control keeps the grep honest, as step 3 does for leak checks.
